title: What If Lightning Struck Your Plane? It Already Does Yearly

scenes.text: What if lightning struck your plane? It already does, about once a year.
The average airliner takes a hit about once a year, roughly every three thousand flight hours.
The bolt can carry up to 200,000 amps, and the channel can reach 30,000 degrees Celsius.
Planes even attract it: flying through a storm's electric field makes a strike about a thousand times likelier than chance.
The metal skin carries the current along the outside. Fuel tanks, joints and wiring are built and tested against it.
Passengers get a flash and a bang. For the plane, it's an ordinary day, then an inspection.
